key_insight: Geometry-based molecular fragmentation enables multiscale polymer representations without predefined chemical fragmentation rules.
engineering_relevance: Combining polymer sequence notation with 3D structural information can improve prediction of several polymer properties.
method: Partition structures using radius-constrained optimization inspired by k-center, with fragment count determined by the radius.
Vary the radius to construct multiscale fragments and integrate them through geometric fragment-based attention.
Combine p-SMILES representations with 3D conformational information in a multimodal model.
evidence_signal: On a benchmark polymer dataset, incorporating 3D conformational information improved prediction accuracy for several properties over p-SMILES-only models; explainability analyses examined physical relevance.
watch_item: The abstract does not quantify performance gains or establish robustness to conformer selection and fragmentation radius.
paper_title: Towards Multiscale Molecular Representation Learning through Geometry-Based Fragmentation for Polymer Property Prediction
